messages:
sandeep: Quick profile run for the streamed workload — seeing recurring micro‑spikes when partial-decode flushes coincide with kernel selection changes. Tail shows ~1.2–2.0ms added per request when a kernel handoff happens during a stream chunk.

sandeep: sample timeline (truncated):
```
[0ms ] accept request A (stream)
[5ms ] accept request B (batchable)
[12ms] partial-decode flush A => triggers send
[13ms] kernel switch to small-kernel for A -> B scheduled -> 1.8ms stall
[15ms] KV cache miss for A's context fetch -> extra 0.6ms
```

maya: ugh. so small-kernel wins for tiny streams and we pay the handoff tax. Did you try preferring existing kernel affinity? :thinking:

sandeep: yeah that's my thinking — two knobs: 1) admission/stitch window to coalesce tiny stream chunks into one kernel-friendly batch, and 2) bias admission to prefer the active kernel for N ms to avoid handoffs.

liam: can we do a guarded approach? e.g., hold stream chunk for X ms only if we expect another token or request to arrive, else flush immediately. we don't want to add tail latency for interactive users.

sandeep: exactly. proposal in brief:
- "stitch_window_ms": short (8–16ms) to collect coalescable stream chunks
- "stitch_max_tokens": cap (e.g., 32–64 tokens) to bound latency cost
- priority bypass: mark interactive streams (interactive=true) to bypass or use 0–4ms window
- kernel_affinity_ttl_ms: prefer current kernel for Y ms after a send to avoid churn

liam: sample config?

sandeep: config we shoved into the local harness for a quick experiment:
```json
{
  "stitch_window_ms": 12,
  "stitch_max_tokens": 48,
  "admission_policy": "prefer_existing_kernel",
  "kernel_affinity_ttl_ms": 30,
  "kv_prefetch": true,
  "early_flush_threshold_ms": 40
}
```

jenna: two concerns: fairness and worst‑case p99. If we hold a lot of small requests to stitch, we might reduce throughput but increase p99 for interactive users unless bypass works reliably. Also KV prefetch could hide misses but increases memory pressure.

sandeep: valid. plan for experiment: A/B split on a subset of traffic (10% experiment, 90% control). Metrics to capture:
- p50/p95/p99 generation latency (stream first-byte and final-byte)
- tokens/sec throughput + GPU utilization
- kernel switch count per 10k requests
- KV cache hit ratio and eviction churn
- number of early_flush events

liam: and add a custom trace tag so we can correlate kernel_switch events with stream flush timestamps. suggestion: tracetag=stitch-exp-03

perf-bot: Experiment created: id=stitch-exp-03, traffic=10%, owner=sandeep, start: now, tracetag=stitch-exp-03 :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: Rollback criteria suggested: >10% increase in p95 final-byte latency OR >5% drop in tokens/sec sustained for 5m. Will auto-roll if both conditions hit.

maya: also watch for KV eviction spikes. If stitch increases batch reuse but warms different keys we could thrash. Maybe decrease KVTTL for ephemeral contexts in experiment.

jenna: agree. add metric: kv_evictions_per_minute and kv_avg_lookup_latency.

sandeep: OK I'll launch the 10% split with this config and the tracetag. If we see kernel_switchs drop and p95 improves without p99 regressions, we can widen to 50%. Otherwise we'll narrow window or reduce affinity TTL.

liam: thanks — ping when the dashboard link is live. :+1:

perf-bot: Dashboard: https://internal/dashboards/stitch-exp-03 (instrumented: p50/p95/p99, kernel_switch_rate, kv_hit, throughput)

sandeep: launched. tagging thread with logs as results come in.

jenna: nice. keep an eye on any outlier tenants that are highly bursty — they tend to defeat stitch logic.

sandeep: noted. will run a tenant-level breakdown after 30m.

perf-bot: Experiment started at 2026-03-18T15:02:30Z, id=stitch-exp-03. Monitoring enabled.

ops-bot: Reminder: set manual kill window if we hit infra anomalies.

maya: thanks team — if early signals look good we'll add a microbenchmark suite to validate kernel selection improvements in CI.
